# 2B.7 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** Scholz’s 2024 record is **moderately favorable** for 2B.7. The clearest evidence is on Gaza: he backed an immediate ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, international humanitarian law, and a two-state settlement. On Ukraine, the record is more limited: he consistently framed support as defensive and escalation-limiting, but I found **little direct evidence** of him pursuing formal peace talks or confidence-building measures beyond resisting direct escalation.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Joint Statement on Gaza** | Federal Government | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/joint-statement-from-the-leaders-of-the-united-states-argentina-austria-brazil-bulgaria-canada-colombia-denmark-france-germany-poland-portugal-romania-serbia-spain-thailand-and-the-united-kingdom-on-gaza-2290942 | Scholz joined a statement calling for an immediate ceasefire, unconditional hostage release, protection of civilians, large-scale humanitarian aid, and compliance with international humanitarian law. It also opposed annexation and backed a negotiated two-state outcome. This is the strongest direct evidence for credible ceasefire and lawful settlement support. | 2B.7, 2B.4, 2B.5 |
| **Interview des Bundeskanzlers mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said he had warned against a Rafah ground offensive, insisted that more humanitarian aid had to reach Gaza, and said every arms delivery was carefully assessed in advance. This shows a willingness to restrain escalation and protect civilians when a peaceful or less violent alternative existed. | 2B.7, 2B.4, 2B.1 |
| **Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said Israel has the right to defend itself, but warfare must comply with international humanitarian law and humanitarian aid must reach Gaza on a large scale. He also reiterated support for a two-state solution. This is explicit support for lawful settlement rather than open-ended war. | 2B.7, 2B.4, 2B.3 |
| **Video: Anniversary of the 7 October attack** | Federal Government | 7 Oct 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/media-center/chancellor-kanzler-kompakt-2313552 | Scholz called for a ceasefire one year after the Hamas attack and described the war as a disaster for the Palestinian people. This is indirect but still relevant evidence of continued ceasefire advocacy and post-conflict concern. | 2B.7, 2B.4 |
| **Scholz calls G7 plan to use Russian windfall profits for Ukraine's defence historic** | Reuters | 13 Jun 2024 | https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/scholz-calls-g7-plan-to-use-russian-windfall-profits-for-ukraines-defence-historic/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjQ6bmV3c21sX1ZBMDQyNTEzMDYyMDI0UlAx | Scholz said Russia wanted to outlast support for Ukraine and presented the G7 windfall-profits plan as a necessary response. This is not a peace talk item, but it is relevant because he frames support as leverage for a lawful defensive settlement rather than open-ended escalation. | 2B.7, 2B.6, 2B.1 |
| **Scholz refuses Taurus delivery because Germany must not be drawn into war** | Bundesregierung | 4 Mar 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/chancelier-questions-2024-2265010 | Scholz openly explained the Taurus decision as a boundary on German involvement in the war. This is relevant because it rejects escalation and preserves space for non-German combat and eventual negotiation. | 2B.7, 2B.1, 2B.6 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I found **little direct evidence** that Scholz personally drove formal peace negotiations on Ukraine in 2024.
- I found **no strong evidence** of ceasefire diplomacy beyond Gaza, and no visible record here of confidence-building measures in the classic arms-control sense.
- His support for Ukraine remained robust, so the posture was not neutralism; it was more accurately **defensive support plus selective ceasefire advocacy**.

## Synthesis for 2B.7

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz did pursue credible ceasefires and lawful settlements when possible, especially on Gaza.
- **Why:** he backed ceasefire language, hostage release, humanitarian access, IHL compliance, and a two-state solution.
- **Main gap:** the record is much thinner on Ukraine peace talks and post-conflict reconciliation.
- **Overall:** moderately positive, with strongest evidence in Gaza and much weaker direct evidence on broader peace-process leadership.

## Search gap

- I did **not** find reliable evidence of Scholz leading direct Ukraine peace talks in 2024.
- I also did **not** find substantial evidence of formal confidence-building measures beyond his general escalation restraint and arms-control framing.
